newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Unicao links new Ivory cocoa processing to demand.
newsitem.headline: Unicao links new Ivory cocoa processing to demand.

text.p: Ivory Coast cocoa processor Unicao is moving to raise capacity, but completion of new plant will depend on demand proving sufficient for its present output.
Chief executive Yves Lambelin told a news conference late on Thursday that the firm aimed to raise capacity at its factory in Abidjan by 21,500 tonnes to 86,000 tonnes of raw beans by September 1997.
But he added, "Plans will depend on market perception of products from Unicao's plant."
"We will move on to further investments once we have sold regularly the quantities now produced," he said, referring specifically to the European and U.S. markets.
Unicao is building a second extension as part of a 9.85 billion CFA investment project. A first 21,500-tonne extension came on line in April, raising capacity to 64,500 tonnes of raw beans.
Ivory Coast is keen to process 50 percent of its production locally by 2000, against around 15 percent at present.
Trade sources describe the target of 50 percent as ambitious.
Junior planning and industrial development minister Theophile Ahoua N'Doli was asked during a tour of the Abidjan site whether the government would help local processors.
He said, "We want to play the game of economic liberalisation. But each time the game is not played elsewhere we will take the necessary steps. We aim to process our primary products."
Unicao said in a statement that part of its output was being processed a second time in France. "A part of the mass will be turned into liquid mass at the group's site at Dunkirk," it added.
Chocolate makers used more and more deodorised cocoa butters and added cocoa liquor to give the products a chocolate taste, so mass or liquor quality was paramount, it added.
Unicao's main shareholders are Ivorian cocoa exporter SIFCA and U.S.-based Grace Cocoa, which in February took a 30 percent stake in SIFCA. Swiss trader Intercafco also has a stake.
Ivory Coast's 1995/96 cocoa crop is estimated at 1.2 million tonnes.
